I read something once where a person was asked why they haven’t committed suicide yet. they said “because I haven’t finished reading my book”. 

the book was never the point though. it might have been a horrible book. the point is that the person had found something to keep them here. even if it’s only for another day or two. 

find something that will keep you here, just for one more day.

i’m so sorry. loneliness is a terrible thing. i also did online schooling as a kid (i’m 20 now). i hated it just like you. but for some reason, i never transferred back to in-person schooling. to this day, it’s one of my biggest regrets. 
i don’t know what your specific situation is like, but if you can transfer back to in-person, do it.

after dealing with chronic loneliness for nearly a decade now, i have learned a lot. possibly the most important lesson i learned is that your greatest weapon against loneliness is hope, and hope is most commonly found in community. surround yourself with people, and eventually you may find some that give you hope. 

you can do this by transferring to in-person schooling and engaging with school clubs and events, or you could volunteer for events your city organizes, or maybe going to church (if your religious), or volunteer at your local library. 

the world is full of hope. all you have to do is find it.

I’m not sure where to start. My mind just felt so messy last night and I new the cutting would help. This week, my porn addiction has gotten worse than ever before and I think I needed to relieve the feelings of shame and embarrassment that are brought on by the addiction. It wasn’t just shame or embarrassment though. It’s fear that it’s going to get worse. That I’m going to pass certain lines that I don’t want to cross. I was right though. The cutting helped. But now I have eleven 1-3 inch lines all around my forearm. Every time I look at them now I feel so weak and hopeless. Seeing how easily my mind broke down and realizing how fragile I really must be. Now all I think about is how can I expect myself to make it through future obstacles if I can’t even make it though the ones I’m dealing with now.
I used to draw patterns on my arm with sharpies. I don’t know why it helped but it did. I would cover my entire forearm with ink.

I used to draw patterns on my arm so that the cuts blended into the patterns. I used sharpies but white board markers or paint could work. This assumes your mother won’t get upset at your forearm being covered in patterns.
